I merged [PR #891](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/891) (day types, flight blocks and meal blocks) after your "lgtm 891". Both CI checks had passed on its latest commit, and I restarted my branch from the new main.

I've started the "Who's coming?" PR on that branch; nothing is pushed yet, and the page code hasn't been run in a browser yet. So far:

- **Spec:** new section 29 with three requirements. "Who's coming?" becomes the first chip: just me, a couple, family with the children's ages, or friends. Your answer suggests how full a day is, which kinds are favoured, when the evening ends and how to eat. A question you've answered yourself is never overwritten.
- **Suggestions:** these follow my earlier proposal. For example, a family with a child under 8 gets an easy pace, family shows, a 21:00 evening and three meals. The full rule is a table in the spec.
- **Page code:** the chip, its ages row, and a "suggested" mark on each chip whose answer was filled in for you. The strings are in all four languages.

Next I'll run the new tests, refresh the screenshots and open the PR. The screenshots will change wherever the chip row shows, because of the sixth chip.

The coordinator has a message for this thread waiting, with a screenshot named "day-end-bug"; it arrives when this turn ends, and I'll read it first.

input.title: PlanNG: who's coming fills in the questions you haven't answered
input.body:
Before: nothing asked who was coming, so every question started at the same default whether a family with a five-year-old was travelling or someone on their own.

After: "Who's coming?" is the first chip, with just me, a couple, family (with the children's ages, as on the Plan2 page) or friends. The answer fills in each question the reader hasn't answered themselves: how full a day is, which kinds are favoured, when the evening ends and how to eat. A filled-in chip shows its answer in italics with a ✨ marked "suggested". Once the reader answers a question, it's theirs, and changing who's coming no longer touches it.

How: `site/planNG/lib/party.js` holds the rule (`suggestedAnswers`), and the table in spec 29.2 is the whole of it. The page tracks which questions the reader answered (`answered` in `planNG.prefs`) and applies suggestions only to the others. The party emoji, and personal time's emoji, are ones the vendored test font already carries.

Spec: new section 29 (29.1–29.3), and 21.1 now lists the sixth chip. Nine goldens that show the chip row were re-rendered.

message.content: This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation. Summary: 1. Primary Request and Intent: - This is Ariel's thread about the PlanNG calendar planning control (site/planNG/). The work runs as a sequence of PRs, in the order Ariel accepted: - (1) Filter bar: PR #885, merged. - (2) Day types, flight blocks and meal blocks: PR #891, merged. - (3) Block look: festival stripe, genre emoji, hatched personal blocks, Free tag. Not started. - (4) Image-first show popover, plus the Haifa/Acco scraper images. Not started. - New asks from Ariel, relayed by the coordinator this session: - (a) The arrival and departure blocks ask how you get to town (car rental, train, taxi), with booking suggestions. A car widens reach, and the travel mode derives from it. - (b) "Who's coming?" from Plan2 (solo/couple/family/friends). Top-level answers derive default answers for unanswered questions (pace, show bias, meals), and an explicit user choice wins. Ariel's words: "top-level preferences derive a slew of different default answers to queststion we haven't asked yet (if we asked and the user chose something else - that's great)". - (c) The year-strip flight markers look tentative until the user settles how they arrive (local, drive own car, train, fly), with no plane prices before that. This is owned by the Annual festivals calendar thread; my arrival choice should share that state, not duplicate it. - (d) Bug: "Wrong scheduling - day end should prevent shows that end after it." Screenshot: shows drawn past "Day ends 20:30". - Decision card: Ariel chose "Start now" for building the follow-up. - Ariel said "lgtm" (merged #885) and "lgtm 891" (merged #891). 2. Key Technical Concepts: - Executable spec in product/requirements.md, with leaves claimed by cases under product/requirements/{screen,behavior,logic}/cases. - Coverage bijection and gallery gates. - Pixel-exact goldens with Playwright 1.56.1. - Doc-first: the spec commit goes first and is red, then the implementation and goldens. - Commands: `npm run test:ui`, `node product/requirements/shared/refresh.js ` (also `npm run refresh:ui `), `npm run verify`. - Retired leaves are deleted and their ids never reused. - Fixture festivals: - Jerusalem (18–22 Oct; trip 17–23 Oct, only Jerusalem in the pool). - Haifa (25 Sep–3 Oct; pools Acco). - Acco (27 Sep–1 Oct; its events have no duration). - Edinburgh. - All are tz Asia/Jerusalem except Edinburgh. - The draft engine is `draftCalendar` in site/plan/lib/contention.js. Pool filtering uses `withinDayWindow` in site/plan/lib/engine.js. A slot with no duration has endMinuteOfDay = startMinuteOfDay. - The vendored emoji font subset is product/requirements/shared/harness/vendor/systemfonts/NotoColorEmoji-req-subset.ttf. Only emoji in it render; others show as tofu. - Rebuilding it from the installed full font changed other goldens, so I reverted and used existing emoji. - The harness's fontconfig cache (os.tmpdir()/edfringe-req-fontconfig) goes stale when a font file is replaced in place. - i18n entries need `probe` + `maxWidthPx`, or `unrendered` + `maxWidthPx: null`, in all four languages (en, he, ru, ja). Every key must appear literally in the source. Localized HTML is generated with `node scripts/localize-pages.mjs`. - The remote branch is auto-deleted after a merge, so push fresh with `git push -u origin claude/project-thread-ct65o2`. - The hearthbot `reply` rejects markdown images; link images instead. - The GitHub merge tool needs the full 40-char sha for expectedHeadSha. 3. Files and Code Sections: - **site/planNG/lib/days.js** (new, merged in #891) - Constants: - `NIGHT_END_MIN = 30*60` - `TRANSFER_MIN = 90` - `AIRPORT_MIN = 150` - `DAY_KINDS = ["rest","excursion","festival"]` - `MEALS` - `seedDay({dates, lead, slots})`: - Picks a nearby festival (not the lead) on its fullest inner day, else rest on the inner day with the fewest only-that-night shows among days with any shows. - Ties go to the earlier day. - Never the first or last day; returns null for trips under 3 days. - `slotRule(kept, busy)`: - Rest/excursion days refuse slots; a festival day refuses other festivals. - Busy intervals use a half-open overlap. - `flightHours(which, flight, dateISO, timeZone)`: - out: `{date, startMin:0, endMin: min(NIGHT_END, landing+90)}`, or null if it lands before the day. - back: `{startMin: max(0, depart-150), endMin: NIGHT_END}`, or null if startMin ≥ NIGHT_END. - Uses Intl wall-clock conversion. - `mealAt(min, has)` returns breakfast (04–11), lunch (11–16), dinner (16–22), otherwise late. If the day already has that meal, it returns "snack". - **site/plan/lib/contention.js** (#891) - Added the option `allowSlot?: (slot)=>boolean`. - In the pool filter, after the pinned check: `if (options.allowSlot && !options.allowSlot(s)) return false; return withinDayWindow(s, dayWindow);` - **site/planNG/planNG.js** (#891) - New state: `kept: Map`, `own: []`, `seededFor`, `mealDates: Set`. Removed d0/d1, the windows storage and window helpers (`tripStartISO/tripEndISO` replace them). - Storage: `KEY_DAYS` ("planNG.days") with saveDays/restoreDays. Days are saved only on reader actions: setKept, drag end, keep drag, add/remove, relayMeals, place change. - Metadata: KEEP_META (rest 😴, excursion 🚌, festival 🎪) and OWN_META (meal; personal ☕ \u2615 after the #893 fix). - Helpers: `keptInTrip`, `flightBlocks`, `busyHours`, `layMeals`, `relayMeals`, `seedDays`, `keptName`, `ownName`, `ownEmoji`. - `planOptions` uses `allowSlot: slotRule(keptInTrip(), busyHours())` in place of mealBreaks. `redraft` calls seedDays() and layMeals() first. - renderCalendar draws the kept block (rest/excursion) or banner (festival, `data-festival-colour`), own/flight blocks (`ownBlock`), head `[data-day-head]`, and zones. The empty-day collapse is skipped when a day has kept or own items. - calendarAxis includes own blocks, the out flight's endMin and the back flight's startMin. - Removed dateEdge, placeDateEdges, layoutOverlay/paintWindow/wireWindow and #win. - Menus: `calMenu()` creates #calMenu (`.cal-pop.cal-menu`). Functions `openDayMenu`, `openAddMenu`, `openOwnMenu`, `setKept`. - Drag: `dragOwn` (move/resize via `.own-resize`, freezes the axis via state.drag, a click opens the own menu), `dragKeep`, `suppressClick`. - `wireDays()` handles pointerdown, click (head / empty body or zone → add menu with a `.sch-add-anchor`), keydown, and the calMenu click. - refreshFares redrafts when the flights change. - Food answer, meal toggle and times call relayMeals. - **#893 additions to planNG.js** - Import `{ AGES, PARTIES, suggestedAnswers }` from "./lib/party.js". - State: `party: null`, `answered: new Set()`; both saved in prefs and restored. - PARTY_META: - solo 🎒 \u{1F392} - couple 🍷 \u{1F377} - family 🧒 \u{1F9D2} - group 🍺 \u{1F37A} - The unset chip answer shows 📝 \u{1F4DD} with "Tell us". - `SUGGESTED = ["pace","interests","food"]` and `isSuggested(q)`. - `whoAnswer`, `whoHtml` (picks plus `.pref-ages` with `[data-age]` buttons). - `applySuggestions()` sets pace, interests, dayEndMin and food for unanswered questions. It is called at boot after restorePrefs and from `whoChanged()`. - questionHtml adds the `is-suggested` class and a `✨` inside pref-ask. syncPrefs toggles is-suggested; `lit.who`. - The click handler handles `[data-age]` and `who:` picks, and marks answered: interests, pace, food. The change handler marks answered pace on data-num and food on mealon/time. `setDayEnd` marks answered "dayEnd". - The "who" chip is first in renderPrefs. - **site/planNG/lib/party.js** (new, #893) ```js export const PARTIES = ["solo","couple","family","group"]; export const AGES = [3,5,7,9,12,15]; const LATE_MIN = 25*60; export function suggestedAnswers(party) { if (!party || !PARTIES.includes(party.type)) return null; if (party.type === "family") { const youngest = ages.length? min : null; small=<8; school=<12; return { pace: small?"easy":"steady", interests:["family"], dayEndMin: small?21*60: school?22*60:LATE_MIN, food:"regular" }; } return { pace: solo?"packed":"steady", interests:[], dayEndMin: LATE_MIN, food: couple?"dinner":"self" }; } ``` - **site/planNG/planNG.css** - #891: removed the window/dateedge/sch-day--out/sch-meal CSS. Added `.sch-keep`, `.sch-keep--festival`, `.keep-label`, `.sch-own` (+ `--meal`, `--flight`, `--out`), `.own-label`, `.own-time`, `.own-resize`, `.sch-add-anchor`, `.cal-menu` and menu items, and `.sch-day-head[data-day-head]` cursor/hover. Flight label wraps. - #893: `.pref-suggested` (hidden unless `.pref.is-suggested`), italic suggested answer, `.pref-ages`/`.pref-ages-label`/`.pref-age`; chip min-width lowered to 132px. - **site/planNG/i18n/translations.js** - #891: removed rail.from/to/startLabel/endLabel. Added meal.late, meal.snack, day.menuLabel (unrendered), day.shows/rest/excursion/festival (probe .keep-label), own.personal, own.remove, flight.arrive ("Landed, free {time}"), flight.depart ("To the airport {time}"). - #893: prefs.who.q/unset/solo/couple/family/group/ages, and prefs.suggested (unrendered). - **site/planNG/index.html** (+he/ru/ja, generated): #win overlay removed. - **product/requirements.md** - #891: 21.1 intro "day's two hour lines"; 21.5 reworded (meal blocks); 21.8 removed; 21.9 notes; section 28 (28.1–28.8) inserted before "## 25."; the fares banner path restored to api/fares.js. - #893: 21.1 statement adds "who's coming", with the notes "nobody said yet"; section 29 (29.1–29.3) inserted before "## 25.". - **Cases** - #891: - screen: jerusalem-rest-day.28.1, planng-festival-day.28.2, jerusalem-flight-days.28.5 - logic: planng-seed-day.28.3, planng-flight-hours.28.6, planng-meal-name.28.8 - behavior: jerusalem-days.28.4, jerusalem-own-blocks.28.7 (scrollIntoView center to avoid the sticky header) - jerusalem-window.21.8 deleted; jerusalem-prefs.21.9 drops the dateedge and windows steps - case-helpers: removed the dateedge wait from jerusalemReady; added `jerusalemAllDays()`, which returns `{"planNG.days": JSON.stringify({kept:{}, own:[], seededFor:"2026-10-17/2026-10-23", mealDates:[]})}`. # The requirements harness

The framework conventions are the `executable-requirements` pack and the judgment layer is
`spec-driven-product` plus the `writing-tests` skill; layout, lanes and commands are
`product/requirements/README.md`. This carries what those don't: a Playwright golden harness,
and the local approval and fixture policy.

## Writing the spec

- **Laying out `product/requirements.md`** — under each visual leaf its golden is visible and
  uncollapsed; every textual expansion (acceptance notes, proof pointers) is collapsed in a
  `<details>` block. The document is read by sight.

- **Writing a visual leaf's statement** — one line saying what is asserted; the golden carries
  the copy, counts, colours and placement. Anything not visible (a threshold, the rule behind
  the state) goes in a collapsed **Notes** block. (visual-leafs-statement)

- **Choosing a golden's capture** — the smallest surface that proves the leaf: an element crop,
  a clipped region, or a stitched composite, never the whole page or control. The recipe lives on
  the case (`capture: "<selector>"` or `capture(page, tools)`, see `shared/capture-tools.js`);
  whole-page capture is a deliberate exception. (golden-smallest-surface)

- **Proving what an action changes** — capture the same region before and after (and after a
  reload where persistence is the point) and play them as one animated golden (`tools.animate`);
  keep `stitchV`/`stitchH` for things genuinely side by side. (change-time-animation)

- **Encoding an animated golden** — APNG, never GIF (`shared/png.js`'s `encodeAnimated`); the
  comparator compares an animated golden's bytes only. (animated-golden-apng)

- **Placing a leaf both pages follow** — the spec is organised by what the product does, never by
  code layout: a cross-page rule is one feature whose picture shows both the Now page and the
  planner, in the cross-page part after the two page-by-page segments. A case may navigate
  between pages, or open a second page when something fixed at context creation must differ.

- **About to route a leaf to `behavior` or `logic`** — first ask whether it decomposes into
  observable states; a statement joined by "and" usually does, and each part becomes its own
  numbered sub-leaf with its own picture, the parent a heading. When a leaf lands in a coded kind
  because the product makes it invisible, say so in its Notes and name the product change that
  would make it visual.

- **Using `behavior`** — for a gesture's outgoing consequence (a URL built, bytes downloaded,
  storage written) or what the OS paints rather than the page (a native `title` tooltip, a
  cursor). (behavior-rule)

- **Using `logic`** — for a pure rule with no rendered surface; when it is about how values are
  written, declare `table: { columns, rows }` so the gallery renders the table and `verify()`
  proves every row. (logic-rule)

## The browser is part of the expected

- **Bumping the pinned Playwright** — it re-renders every golden, so it is a re-baselining,
  approved like one: the harness refuses any other version (`shared/harness/browser.js`).

- **A comparison that flaps** — add determinism, never a tolerance; the comparator stays at zero
  diff, and the levers (fixed clock, geolocation, seeded `Math.random`, route-fulfilled network,
  frozen animations, render flags) all live in the harness.

## Traps the harness already paid for

- **Serving the fake origin** — keep it `https://`: geolocation exists only on secure origins,
  and on plain http the app keeps its simulated clock and renders the wrong day.
  (geolocation-exists-only)

- **Moving or denying the fixed geolocation** — the app adopts the device clock only on an
  in-UK fix, so anywhere else renders its pre-set simulated moment, a different day file.
  (app-adopts-device)

- **Captures racing the planner's board animation** — a CSS freeze doesn't stop
  `element.animate`; the harness stubs it to land on end states. (css-freeze-does)

- **Text shifting by a pixel everywhere** — the vendored `fonts.css` resolves against
  `fonts.googleapis.com`, so the vendor route matches on path, host-agnostic. (fonts-arrive-google)

- **Adding an emoji, symbol or script to the product or fixtures** — rebuild the
  `harness/vendor/systemfonts/` subset (its README): Chromium runs under a `FONTCONFIG_FILE`
  that sees only that directory, and a missing glyph renders as tofu. (vendoring-web-fonts)

- **Reproducing a golden flake locally** — compare with the harness's `compare.js`, never a byte
  hash: PNG bytes differ across identical renders, and CI enforces pixels.
  (reproducing-golden-flake)

- **A red `ui-requirements` lane** — its artifact downloads from a host the proxy denies, so read
  which case failed from `get_job_logs` (large `tail_lines`) and re-run it locally;
  `npm run test:ui` writes `.actual.png` / `.diff.png` into `shared/.artifacts/`. (red-ci-lanes)

- **Capturing a floating popup** — set `viewportOnly: true`: a full-page capture scrolls, and
  scrolling dismisses tips, legends and pops. (floating-popup-dies)

- **Waiting for a page to be ready** — wait on the observable state the pages settle into (the
  footer version popup's text, the search placeholder's show count; `case-helpers.js`) plus
  `document.fonts.ready`, never `networkidle`. (ready-networkidle)

- **Capturing hover-driven UI** — open it inside `capture()`, not `drive()`: the runner settles
  the scroll between them, and the scroll fires `mouseleave`. (hover-driven-ui)

## The fixture freeze

- **Needing data for a case** — use `shared/fixtures/data/`, a frozen snapshot of the real
  committed data cast by the committed builder for state variety; never reach for `site/data/`.
  Every deviation from the source bytes is an `ADJUST` in the builder.

- **Re-running the builder** — it re-casts every golden, so run it only with the owner's
  approval and land builder, fixtures, goldens and gallery in one reviewed change.

- **Having invoked `build-fixtures.js` at all**, even against a scratch edit — it writes into
  `fixtures/data/` as it goes, so `git diff --stat` the whole fixtures dir before deciding there
  is nothing to revert. (build-fixtures-partial-drift)

## Golden approval

- **A golden that no longer matches** — show the owner the committed golden beside
  `shared/.artifacts/<case>.actual.png` and `.diff.png` through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, one
  per item, and say so in the PR body.

- **Landing an intended UI change** — spec edit (doc-first, red), then the implementation, then
  `npm run refresh:ui`, with the refreshed PNGs in the same diff.

  observable states; a statement joined by "and" usually does, and each part becomes its own
  numbered sub-leaf with its own picture, the parent a heading. When a leaf lands in a coded kind
  because the product makes it invisible, say so in its Notes and name the product change that
  would make it visual.

- **Using `behavior`** — for a gesture's outgoing consequence (a URL built, bytes downloaded,
  storage written) or what the OS paints rather than the page (a native `title` tooltip, a
  cursor). (behavior-rule)

- **Using `logic`** — for a pure rule with no rendered surface; when it is about how values are
  written, declare `table: { columns, rows }` so the gallery renders the table and `verify()`
  proves every row. (logic-rule)

## The browser is part of the expected

- **Bumping the pinned Playwright** — it re-renders every golden, so it is a re-baselining,
  approved like one: the harness refuses any other version (`shared/harness/browser.js`).

- **A comparison that flaps** — add determinism, never a tolerance; the comparator stays at zero
  diff, and the levers (fixed clock, geolocation, seeded `Math.random`, route-fulfilled network,
  frozen animations, render flags) all live in the harness.

## Traps the harness already paid for

- **Serving the fake origin** — keep it `https://`: geolocation exists only on secure origins,
  and on plain http the app keeps its simulated clock and renders the wrong day.
  (geolocation-exists-only)

- **Moving or denying the fixed geolocation** — the app adopts the device clock only on an
  in-UK fix, so anywhere else renders its pre-set simulated moment, a different day file.
  (app-adopts-device)

- **Captures racing the planner's board animation** — a CSS freeze doesn't stop
  `element.animate`; the harness stubs it to land on end states. (css-freeze-does)

- **Text shifting by a pixel everywhere** — the vendored `fonts.css` resolves against
  `fonts.googleapis.com`, so the vendor route matches on path, host-agnostic. (fonts-arrive-google)

- **Adding an emoji, symbol or script to the product or fixtures** — rebuild the
  `harness/vendor/systemfonts/` subset (its README): Chromium runs under a `FONTCONFIG_FILE`
  that sees only that directory, and a missing glyph renders as tofu. (vendoring-web-fonts)

- **Reproducing a golden flake locally** — compare with the harness's `compare.js`, never a byte
  hash: PNG bytes differ across identical renders, and CI enforces pixels.
  (reproducing-golden-flake)

- **A red `ui-requirements` lane** — its artifact downloads from a host the proxy denies, so read
  which case failed from `get_job_logs` (large `tail_lines`) and re-run it locally;
  `npm run test:ui` writes `.actual.png` / `.diff.png` into `shared/.artifacts/`. (red-ci-lanes)

- **Capturing a floating popup** — set `viewportOnly: true`: a full-page capture scrolls, and
  scrolling dismisses tips, legends and pops. (floating-popup-dies)

- **Waiting for a page to be ready** — wait on the observable state the pages settle into (the
  footer version popup's text, the search placeholder's show count; `case-helpers.js`) plus
  `document.fonts.ready`, never `networkidle`. (ready-networkidle)

- **Capturing hover-driven UI** — open it inside `capture()`, not `drive()`: the runner settles
  the scroll between them, and the scroll fires `mouseleave`. (hover-driven-ui)

## The fixture freeze

- **Needing data for a case** — use `shared/fixtures/data/`, a frozen snapshot of the real
  committed data cast by the committed builder for state variety; never reach for `site/data/`.
  Every deviation from the source bytes is an `ADJUST` in the builder.

- **Re-running the builder** — it re-casts every golden, so run it only with the owner's
  approval and land builder, fixtures, goldens and gallery in one reviewed change.

- **Having invoked `build-fixtures.js` at all**, even against a scratch edit — it writes into
  `fixtures/data/` as it goes, so `git diff --stat` the whole fixtures dir before deciding there
  is nothing to revert. (build-fixtures-partial-drift)

## Golden approval

- **A golden that no longer matches** — show the owner the committed golden beside
  `shared/.artifacts/<case>.actual.png` and `.diff.png` through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, one
  per item, and say so in the PR body.

- **Landing an intended UI change** — spec edit (doc-first, red), then the implementation, then
  `npm run refresh:ui`, with the refreshed PNGs in the same diff.

Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). <?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.
