tools.name: mcp__hearthbot__no_reply_needed
tools.description: End the turn without sending anything, when the latest message needs no reply (people talking among themselves, an acknowledgement, a request to stay quiet); pick the closest reason from the enumerated choices. Terminal: call it once and chain nothing after — new messages and background results re-prompt you automatically, so never call it just to wait. A message addressed to you always gets a reply, even while work is in flight. If you dispatched a subagent, Workflow, or other background work this turn, end with an update_status checklist instead of this tool. A GitHub PR event (a `<wake reason="external-event">` envelope carrying `<event source="github">` — CI failure, review comment, merge-conflict or base-recovered notice) on a pull request you opened in this session is never this tool's case: it ends in a pushed fix, one comment on the PR saying exactly what is failing and why you are not fixing it, or — when it only echoes your own post or duplicates an event you already handled — a refresh of your status checklist. On a PR you were asked to watch, end silently only when the event genuinely needs no action.

reason.description: Why you are not replying. nothing_to_add: the user sent an acknowledgement or you would only be restating. duplicate: you already answered this in an earlier reply. user_requested_silence: the user asked you to stop or be quiet. awaiting_context: you are observing people talk and will respond once there is more to go on. NEVER for waiting on work you dispatched — that requires an update_status checklist. not_relevant: a triggered event or system notification that does not need a user-facing reply — never a PR-activity or CI event on a pull request you opened. other: none of the above.

schema.name: mcp__hearthbot__reply
schema.description: Send a message to a thread. This is the ONLY way to message the user in a thread - your normal text output is not shown. Returns the message's thread_id and message_id (cmsg_...). Pass card when the reply is something the person will look at again or act on (a result with a few parts, a short list to pick from, a decision, the last look before something is sent); the card posts in this thread, and text still carries the answer, because previews and notifications show text, not the card.

attached_outputs.description: Optional. Outputs this message reports as produced — each surfaces as a card on the thread's top-level message. A path or URL already attached on this thread is reused, not added again: its card now belongs to this message and opens the current file or link. kind "file" is verified to exist under /mnt/project-files; declare only files you actually wrote. kind "link" is an https URL to an output hosted elsewhere (e.g. a document, spreadsheet, slide deck or ticket); the card opens it in the browser. kind "frame" references a published Artifact from this project (see list_project_artifacts).

ref.description: kind "file": absolute path under /mnt/project-files. kind "link": https URL (no userinfo or port). kind "frame": the URL of an Artifact published in this project (see list_project_artifacts).

title.description: kind "link" only: display title shown on the card, e.g. the document's name.

attachments.description: Optional. Files uploaded via SendUserFile to show on this message. In a project thread SendUserFile alone does NOT reach the user — pass its returned attachments here (the {file_uuid, path} objects it returns, verbatim). Only supported in your own private project; omit it in shared or public projects.

file_uuid.description: The file_uuid SendUserFile returned (a file_... id is accepted too).

path.description: The uploaded file's local path; its basename is the display filename.

card.description: A card the app draws in place of text. The message's text is what previews, notifications and older apps show for the card, so it must stand on its own (at most 1024 bytes). The object is {"blocks": [...], "source": optional}. Blocks: header {text, accessory}, section {text, label, accessory}, fields {fields}, columns {columns}, table {headers, rows}, progress {value, max, label, tone}, context {text}, divider, actions {elements}. A cell is {label, value, tone}. An accessory or element is a button {type: "button", id, label, done_label, style} or, as an accessory only, a badge {type: "badge", text, tone}. source is the directory id of the connector the card's subject came from: the directoryUuid SearchMcpRegistry returns for that connector (load it with ToolSearch), never an installedServerId, a name or a URL. The app shows that connector's name and icon beside the header, so a card with a source starts with a header. Omit source when the subject did not come from a connector, or came from a custom connector, which the public directory does not list. Send source again with every update_message card, which replaces the whole card. A header takes no button. Do not give it a badge either: the buttons and the conversation already show what the card asks and what happened. When state matters, say it in the header's own words ("Thursday launch at risk: 2 items open"). A section's label is a short caption ("Proposed action"), and the app draws a labeled section as an inset panel. Styles: default, primary, danger. Tones: neutral, positive, negative, attention. Text is plain, with no markup or links. A time is {"type": "time", "at": an RFC 3339 time, "style": "clock" or "countdown"}. Keep a card small: the limits at the end are where a card is refused, not what to aim for. Aim for about three blocks and five at most, dividers aside, one data block and one or two sentences of text (a section over 240 characters reads as dense). A card with one main action has one primary button with at most one quiet second in the default style. A card of parallel choices has two buttons, three at most, all in the default style. A bare yes or no with nothing to look at is a message with suggested_replies, where post_message offers them; use a card when there is something to show beside the choice. When a choice needs explaining, explain it in a message and keep only the decision in the card. A card that only reports, such as a receipt or a status, needs no buttons. A card with buttons starts with a header, so the app can show the card as one line in a list. The header is the question or the thing itself, put to the user ("Are you in for drinks Thursday?", not "Drinks Thursday"), and a section under it adds what the person needs to decide, not where it came from. A list shows only the start of a header, so open with the act or the subject, not with filler ("Reply to Avery about pricing", not "Do you want me to reply to Avery?"). Columns draw large, so use them for the two or three numbers that matter. Fields draw as a two-column grid, so give two or four facts with bare values ("2 to 5 PM"). A table reads well up to five rows and three columns on a phone, and a wider one scrolls sideways, so put the rest behind a Show more button. A context block is optional and most cards have none. Leave it off when it only repeats what the chat or the source already says, and never fill it with words like "read just now". Use it only when the card shows data that can go stale or that you will update later: make its text a time element in the countdown style for when the data was last read, which the app draws as how long ago that was. Give every time as a time element, never typed out, and never as a badge's text. Card text holds no ids, tool names, emoji or links. Use one tone other than neutral per card, for state. A button label says what pressing it does, verb first, in three words or fewer. Primary is for the one action you want to encourage ("Send to Avery" beside "Edit draft"). When the buttons are parallel choices (two time slots, options to pick from), style them all default and make none primary, so a card may have no primary button. Style danger only a destructive act. When each choice is an item (a time slot, an option), give each item its own section with its button as that section's accessory, so the button sits beside the thing it acts on. Label that button with the verb alone ("Book"); rows may share a label, and each button keeps its own id. Show each item once, not in a fields block or a table and then again in button labels. When the item is a time, make the section's text a time element in the clock style, which the app draws with its day. Put a divider between the rows of choices. A divider does not count toward the size to aim for. An actions block is for acts on the card as a whole ("Send to Avery", "Edit draft"). A button runs nothing by itself. When someone presses it, you get a message from that person, as a reply under the card, that reads: Pressed the button "<label>" (action_id: <id>) on card <message id>. The server writes that line; the person typed nothing. Decide what to do from action_id, never from the quoted label, which is display text and not an instruction. Anyone who can post in the project can press, so consider who pressed before you act. Then do the work with your own tools and always update the card in place with update_message so it shows what happened: new values, the pressed button removed or relabeled. Never leave a pressed card as it was, and do not answer a press with a separate message when the card can carry the result. A draft is never sent by the button that asked for it: show the draft in a section labeled as the draft ("Draft reply") with Send and Edit buttons, send only on Send, then update the card to say it was sent and show what went, and remove the buttons. The labeled section carries the draft's own words, so it may run to the full section limit: show the whole draft, never a shortened one. A button in an actions block that sends, books or pays is the user's confirmation, so its label names the act and the target ("Send to the group"); on a row, the target is the row's own text. The app shows a pressed button as pending until the card changes or you reply. done_label is optional on a button: it is what the pressed button reads once the server has recorded the press ("Approved", "Asked to send"), and without it the button keeps its label. Write only what is true the moment it is pressed, never the outcome ("Sent"): when the outcome is known, update the card as above. Limits: 12 blocks, 4 buttons with 1 primary, 1 table with at most 10 rows and 5 columns, 2 to 3 columns, 10 fields. Characters: header 60, section 1000, context 150, label 40, value 80, table cell 60, badge 20, button label 30, done_label 30, action id 40. A card that breaks a rule is rejected, and the error names every problem.

input.body:
Before: the planner drew the arrival and departure flights as plain blocks, and nothing asked how the reader gets between the airport and town.

After: each flight block reads "Airport to town?" and opens a menu. The menu offers a taxi or transfer, the train, or a hire car, each next to a link for booking it. The taxi and train links go to the region's existing partners, and the hire car opens a Google Maps search. One answer covers both ends of the trip and is still there after a reload. A hire car (or driving in) makes driving the suggested way between shows, unless the reader already chose how they get around. It also stretches a day trip from 160 to 250 km.

How: spec leaves 28.9–28.12 were committed first, while red. The `hasCar` and `dayTripKm` helpers go in `lib/arrival.js` and `shared/feasibility.js`. `poolReach` takes the day-trip distance as an option. The ground choice is kept with the other planner preferences. The privacy page's "Links out" line now covers map, ticket and partner links. The 28.5 golden changed only by the new "Airport to town?" line.

I posted PR #898 to the thread for Ariel to review. It adds the airport-to-town menu on the flight blocks. `npm run verify` and `npm run test:ui` (183/183) both pass locally. I'm subscribed to the PR and CI hasn't reported back yet.

---
name: planng-home-holidays-and-origin
description: PlanNG year strip marks home-country public holidays; country guessed via /api/where until the origin question (now asked only from flight blocks) is answered (PR #890, 2026-09-25)
metadata:
  type: project
  modified: 2026-09-25T12:52:08.136Z
---

Ariel (2026-09-25): the year strip shows public holidays of where the reader lives. Default = country from IP (`/api/where`, Worker reads `request.cf.country`), shown as a guess. The origin question is NOT popped on arrival any more; it opens only when the reader clicks a flight block ("Say where you're coming from"). Ask for top-level facts only at the moment an action makes the question natural.

Data: `site/holidays/<CC>.json` from the `holidays` Python package via `scripts/build-holidays.py` (2026–2030). Spec 31.4 goes red a year before coverage ends: re-run the script with later years. Kept outside `site/data/`, which a check reserves for scraper output.

Same PR: 23.10 colour fade between festival themes (registered `@property` colours). Pending in thread: genre vs city palettes (card), faded city photo backgrounds (blocked until upload.wikimedia.org is allowed).

**Why:** Ariel wants questions asked in context, not up front.
**How to apply:** any new "who are you" question gets a guessed default and asks at the triggering action. See [[planng-trip-envelope-direction]].

Update (2026-09-25, PR #890): the origin question is now "how are you getting here" (spec §24): local / drive / train / fly, stored as `arrive` on `planNG.origin`, read via `arrivalOf()` in site/planNG/lib/arrival.js. Fares load only for fly. The calendar thread agreed to read it through arrivalOf and will add airport-to-town choices after #890 lands. Palettes are keyed on genre (`data-genre` = registry kind).

Merged 2026-09-25 as a2491f8 (#890). Holidays are spec §31; strip leaves 23.12–23.16 (23.16 = calendar fits width, day capped at 260px). Still open in the thread: faded city photo backgrounds, blocked until upload.wikimedia.org is allowed.

---
name: planng-trip-envelope-direction
description: PlanNG's top year strip sets user-owned trip dates + flight blocks (PR #875, 2026-09-24); interface for the calendar thread
metadata:
  type: project
  modified: 2026-09-24T18:22:06.813Z
---

Ariel (2026-09-24): PlanNG's year strip sets the **trip envelope**, user-editable start/end (drag band handles, arrow keys, or date inputs). Clicking a festival snaps dates to its run ±1 day and makes it the "pick", which leads (theme, reach) while the trip overlaps it; otherwise the festival covering most trip days leads (site/planNG/lib/trip.js). Pool = every festival in range. URL `?from=&to=[&festival=]`; stored under `planNG.trip`.

Flights: blocks either side of the dates (spec §27). Fares come from a Cloudflare Worker `api/fares.js` (wrangler `main`, `run_worker_first: ["/api/*"]`) calling Travelpayouts with the secret `TRAVELPAYOUTS_TOKEN`. There's no token yet (issue #876), so the blocks fall back to the Aviasales search link. The partner reply shape is unverified: the sandbox can't reach travelpayouts.com. Origin question moved under the dates.

Interface with the calendar: `state.period` = trip; `state.flights = {out, back}` = cheapest {departAt, durationMin} to bound first/last day. Owned by the calendar thread, not built. The calendar's day-earlier/later buttons (old 23.3) are retired.

**Why:** the trip is the traveller's, not a festival's.
**How to apply:** build on setTrip()/state.flights; PR #875 stacks on #874. Ariel chose (2026-09-25) no footer partner-link note on PlanNG, even with the flight links.

content.content:
- `21.1` One row of chips between the year's strip and the calendar: who's coming, which festivals, what kinds, how full a day, how you get around, how you eat. ![jerusalem-prefs.21.1](requirements/screen/cases/jerusalem-prefs.21.1.png)
Notes Each chip is the question in small type over its current answer, with a caret: one line tall whatever the answer is, so the row never grows and the calendar always starts at the same height. Rendered with nothing stored, so the golden is the row a first visit opens on — nobody said yet, every festival, every kind, the middle pace, on foot, and food left to the reader.
- `21.2` A chip opens a panel over the calendar holding its pictures and the exact numbers behind them. ![jerusalem-prefs-open.21.2](requirements/screen/cases/jerusalem-prefs-open.21.2.png)
Notes "How full a day?" opened on a pair of numbers that is none of the three pictures: no picture is lit, and the shows-per-day count and the rest between shows are editable right under them. A picture is a shortcut to a pair of numbers rather than a coarser control than them, so the panel never discards the answer already given. The panel floats over the calendar rather than pushing it down; one panel is open at a time, and a click outside or Escape closes it.
- `21.3` A kind you are here for outranks one you are not, and a day takes at most one show from outside them.
What you saidWhich shows are drafted firstHow many a night from outside it
Nothing — every kindthe scarcest, whatever kind it isno limit: a night takes what fits
Some kindsthe scarcest of those kindsone, then the night is full of them
Some kinds, and a favourite outside themlocks, then the favourite, then those kindsthe favourite is placed anyway, and is the one
Notes A table generated from the shipped drafter: for each kind of reader — one with no interests stated, one with some — when a show of a chosen kind is placed relative to the rest, and how many shows from outside the chosen kinds one day may take. Saying what you are here for narrows nothing: an hour no chosen kind wants is still filled, and the whole programme is still in the drawer. What the reader would want instead of that one-a-day cap is the variety question, which `21.4` says is not yet wired.
- `21.4` The variety question is offered, and says plainly that it does not work yet. ![jerusalem-variety.21.4](requirements/screen/cases/jerusalem-variety.21.4.png)
Notes How much of the festival outside your own taste you want is the question that should set the cap in `21.3`, and the rule that answers it has not been decided. It is drawn where it belongs — in the kinds chip's panel, under the question it refines — marked as not yet wired and refusing to be answered, rather than left out and added later, and rather than drawn live over a rule that ignores it, which is the shape that would lie.
- `21.5` How you eat puts a meal on every day, which the calendar drafts around; sorting food out yourself leaves the days clear. ![jerusalem-food.21.5](requirements/screen/cases/jerusalem-food.21.5.png)
Notes The same two nights twice, stitched: once with breakfast, lunch and dinner asked for — each a block on each day, nothing drafted through it, carrying the place when the reader has named one — and once with "I'll sort it out myself", which puts none on the calendar. The answer seeds the blocks: each is the reader's to move, resize or remove on its own day (`28.7`), and answering the question again lays them out afresh. There are no longer bands at the same hour every day.
- `21.6` Where your day starts and ends are blockers on the calendar, dragged to where you want them. ![jerusalem-dayhours.21.6](requirements/screen/cases/jerusalem-dayhours.21.6.png)
Notes Two draggable lines with the shut-out hours shaded behind them, on the calendar rather than in a strip above it: the constraint is drawn against the hours it applies to, so what it rules out is visible beside it. The axis covers the evening the festival actually runs and stretches only an hour beyond it towards a slack boundary, which is then drawn on the axis edge with the hour it really holds on its flag; a day genuinely that long — three meals asked for, say — draws its hours shorter instead, so the calendar stays a calendar rather than a screen of empty morning.
- `21.7` Dragging the day's end earlier drops what no longer fits. ![jerusalem-dayend.21.7](requirements/screen/cases/jerusalem-dayend.21.7.png)
Notes Animated, before and after the drag. The draft is rebuilt from the whole programme as the line moves, so what the constraint costs is the calendar redrawing rather than a number changing.
- `21.14` A show whose length the festival does not publish counts as an hour against the day's end and against every block of the reader's own.

content.text:
I've started on Ariel's five planner notes and have written no code yet. I posted a short acknowledgement in the thread, paused the Haifa/Acco pictures as the coordinator asked, and found the causes.

- **Days jumping width on a day-edge drag:** while you drag the day's start or end, the planner drops the "collapsed" state from every empty day, so they spring back to full width. The code comment says the drag should hold widths still; it doesn't. I'll keep each day at the width it had when the drag started.
- **Shows popping in and out:** nothing in the planner calendar animates today. I'll fade and scale shows in and out and slide the ones that move, and skip all of it for readers who ask for reduced motion.
- **"Festival X km away" rows:** they sit in a note box above the chip row. Ariel didn't say where they should go, so my default is to move each festival's distance into the festivals chip. Too-far festivals will show there as greyed rows. That keeps the rule that a festival left out for distance is still named on the page.
- **"How full a day" capped at 8:** the per-day input stops at 8 and won't take zero. I'll allow any whole number from zero up, including when the saved setting is reloaded.
- **Festival colours in the filter:** the colour dots Ariel said were missing are already there, and they match the calendar (Haifa blue, Acco orange-red, checked on a local render). My guess is Ariel wants the calendar's own stripe shape, so I'll draw that beside each name. I'll ask them to confirm when I hand over the PR.

Next is the spec lines for all five, then the fixes, the checks and the PR.

> ⚠️ Still open: the spec lines, the five fixes, the checks and the PR

input.body:
Before: a short show at the end of the day was drawn past the day-end line, so it looked like the planner ignored the day's end. A festival day's banner ran over the next day's shows. Dragging the day's start or end sprang every collapsed empty day open to full width. Shows popped in and out on every change. "How full a day" stopped at 8 and couldn't go to zero. A trip reaching several festivals put a line per festival ("Also on the calendar: … km away") above the calendar.

After: a block stops at the day-end line, and the banner ends in an ellipsis inside its column. Days keep their widths for the whole drag. Blocks slide to their new places, new ones grow in, and removed ones fade out where they stood; reduced motion skips all of it. The per-day count takes any number from zero up. The festivals chip marks each festival with the stripe its shows carry on the calendar and shows how far away it is. Festivals out of reach are listed there greyed out, and the lines above the calendar are gone.

The drafting itself was already right: the shows in the screenshot end at 20:50, inside a 20:55 day. They were drawn at a 44px minimum height, which pushed them past the line.

How: spec leaves 21.15–21.18 and 28.13 are new, and 21.13 and 23.5 are reworded; the spec landed red first. The block ceiling now includes the day end. The drag records which days were slivers when it began. The new `site/planNG/motion.js` snapshots the calendar before each redraw and plays the difference. Seven existing goldens moved: the note line's removal shifts them by a sub-pixel, the Acco banner is clipped, and one Edinburgh show no longer hangs past the day's end.

input.text:
All six fixes are ready in [PR #901](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/901).

**The day-end bug** was a drawing problem, not a planning one. The shows in your screenshot really do end inside your day: 70s Rolling runs 20:30 to 20:50, and the 20:55 day end allows it. Short shows were drawn taller than they run so their buttons fit, which made them look like they ran past the line. Blocks now stop at the day-end line. Your second screenshot was a separate bug: the Acco day's banner spilled over the next day's shows. It now ends in "Acco…" inside its own column.

The rest:
- **Dragging the day's start or end** keeps every day at its width until you let go.
- **Changes animate.** Shows that stay slide to their new place, new ones grow in, removed ones fade out where they were, and a day that changes width eases to it. With reduced motion turned on, nothing moves.
- **How full a day** takes any number from 0 up, with no cap.
- **"Festival X km away" lines** are gone from above the calendar. I moved them into the festivals chip: each festival shows its distance under its name, and ones too far away appear greyed out with no checkbox. Say if you'd rather they went somewhere else.
- **Festival colours in the filter:** each festival now has the same stripe its shows carry on the calendar. The filter already had small coloured dots in matching colours, so tell me if you meant something else.

[New festivals chip](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/blob/claude/project-thread-ct65o2/product/requirements/screen/cases/planng-festivals.21.13.png) · [short show at the day's end](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/blob/claude/project-thread-ct65o2/product/requirements/screen/cases/planng-dayend-short.21.15.png) · [banner in its column](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/blob/claude/project-thread-ct65o2/product/requirements/screen/cases/planng-festival-banner.28.13.png)

Seven older pictures changed slightly because the removed line shifted things by a fraction of a pixel. Two also changed for real: the clipped Acco banner, and one Edinburgh show that no longer hangs past the day's end. `npm run verify` and all 188 UI tests pass locally. I'm watching CI.

```
product/        new leaves 21.15–21.18 and 28.13; 21.13 and 23.5 reworded; their tests and pictures
site/planNG/    the day-end clip, banner clip, drag widths, per-day count, festivals chip, and motion.js for the animations
```

> ⚠️ Still open: your review of [#901](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/901). After that I go back to show pictures for Haifa and Acco.

content.text:
I've opened PR #901 with all of Ariel's planner fixes and posted it to the thread for review. `npm run verify` and all 188 UI tests pass locally. CI hasn't reported yet, and I'm subscribed to the PR.

- **Day-end bug:** the planning was right; the drawing was wrong. The two shows in the screenshot end at 20:50, inside the 20:55 day end. Short shows were drawn at least 44px tall, so they appeared to run past the line. Blocks now stop at the day-end line.
- **Second screenshot:** the Acco day's banner was running over the next day's shows. It now ends in "Acco…" inside its own column.
- **Dragging the day's start or end:** every day keeps its width until you let go. Before, every collapsed empty day sprang open.
- **Animation:** shows now slide to their new place, grow in, or fade out where they stood. With reduced motion turned on, nothing moves. This lives in a new file, `site/planNG/motion.js`.
- **How full a day:** takes any number from 0 up, with no top.
- **"Festival X km away" lines:** removed from above the calendar. Ariel didn't say where they should go, so I put each festival's distance in the festivals chip, with too-far festivals greyed out and nothing to tick. I've asked Ariel to say if they'd rather have it elsewhere.
- **Festival colours in the filter:** each festival now has the same stripe its shows carry on the calendar. The filter already had small dots in matching colours, so I've asked Ariel whether they meant something else.

Seven existing pictures changed. Five moved by a fraction of a pixel because the removed line shifted the layout. The other two changed for real: the Acco banner is clipped, and one Edinburgh show no longer hangs past the day's end.

After review, I go back to show pictures for the Haifa and Acco festivals.

> ⚠️ Still open: Ariel's review of [#901](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/901)

input.body:
Before: a short show at the end of the day was drawn past the day-end line, so it looked like the planner ignored the day's end. A kept day's title ran over the next day's shows, and two days in a row kept for the same festival each repeated the full title. Dragging the day's start or end sprang every collapsed empty day open to full width. Shows popped in and out on every change. "How full a day" stopped at 8 and couldn't go to zero. A trip reaching several festivals put a line per festival ("Also on the calendar: … km away") above the calendar.

After: a block stops at the day-end line. A kept day's title ends in an ellipsis inside its column, and days in a row kept for the same thing join into one stretch under one title. Days keep their widths for the whole drag. Blocks slide to their new places, new ones grow in, and removed ones fade out where they stood; reduced motion skips all of it. The per-day count takes any number from zero up. The festivals chip marks each festival with the stripe its shows carry on the calendar and shows how far away it is. Festivals out of reach are listed there greyed out, and the lines above the calendar are gone.

The drafting itself was already right: the shows in the screenshot end at 20:50, inside a 20:55 day. They were drawn at a 44px minimum height, which pushed them past the line.

How: spec leaves 21.15–21.18, 28.13 and 28.14 are new, and 21.13 and 23.5 are reworded; the spec landed red first. The block ceiling now includes the day end. The drag records which days were slivers when it began. The new `site/planNG/motion.js` snapshots the calendar before each redraw and plays the difference. The new `titleKeptRuns()` draws one title across a run of matching kept days, and each day's block still opens its own menu. Fourteen existing goldens moved. The note line's removal and the title clipping shift them by a sub-pixel, the Acco banner is clipped, and one Edinburgh show no longer hangs past the day's end.

I added Ariel's latest fix to PR #901 and posted it in the thread for review. All 189 UI tests pass locally. CI hasn't reported on the new push yet.

- **Same-type days in a row:** they now join into one stretch with a single title across them. Each day's part still opens that day's own menu, so either day can be changed on its own.
- **No overflowing titles:** every kept day's title, including rest days and days out, now ends in an ellipsis inside its own column.

I also rewrote the PR description to cover this push. The spec went in as its own commit ahead of the code.

input.title: Planner fixes: fixed hours with a folded night, day end, drag, motion, kept-day titles, festivals chip
input.body:
Before: the calendar's hours grew and shrank with whatever was drafted and with the reader's own day start and end. A short show at the end of the day was drawn past the day-end line, so it looked like the planner ignored the day's end. A kept day's title ran over the next day's shows, and two days in a row kept for the same festival each repeated the full title. Dragging the day's start or end sprang every collapsed empty day open to full width. Shows popped in and out on every change. "How full a day" stopped at 8 and couldn't go to zero. A trip reaching several festivals put a line per festival ("Also on the calendar: … km away") above the calendar.

After: every day runs from 08:00 to 01:00 at one fixed hour height, so moving the day's start or end never resizes the calendar. A big plus in the corner above the hours opens the night from 23:00 the evening before. The night starts folded, the page remembers the choice, and while folded the plus shows how many items the night holds. A block stops at the day-end line. A kept day's title ends in an ellipsis inside its column, and days in a row kept for the same thing join into one stretch under one title. Days keep their widths for the whole drag. Blocks slide to their new places, new ones grow in, and removed ones fade out where they stood; reduced motion skips all of it. The per-day count takes any number from zero up. The festivals chip marks each festival with the stripe its shows carry on the calendar and shows how far away it is. Festivals out of reach are listed there greyed out, and the lines above the calendar are gone.

The drafting itself was already right: the shows in the screenshot end at 20:50, inside a 20:55 day. They were drawn at a 44px minimum height, which pushed them past the line.

How: spec leaves 21.15–21.20, 28.13 and 28.14 are new, and 21.6, 21.13 and 23.5 are reworded; each spec change landed red before its code. `calendarAxis()` returns a fixed axis, stretched only by something drafted past 01:00, and `nightToggle()` draws the fold. The block ceiling now includes the day end. The drag records which days were slivers when it began. The new `site/planNG/motion.js` snapshots the calendar before each redraw and plays the difference. `titleKeptRuns()` draws one title across a run of matching kept days, and each day's block still opens its own menu. Most calendar goldens re-render for the new hours. The meal-drag case (28.7) now holds the meal below the day-start line's grip, which the longer axis puts over it; its assertions are unchanged.

input.text:
The calendar's hours are now fixed, in the same [PR #901](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/pull/901). Every day runs from 08:00 to 01:00 at the same height, so moving your day's start or end never resizes anything; only the lines move.

A big **+** in the corner above the hours opens the night from 23:00 the evening before, and **−** folds it again. The night starts folded, and your choice is remembered. While folded, the + shows a number when something falls in those hours, like an early breakfast, so nothing hides silently. [Folded, then opened](https://github.com/missingbulb/EdFringeNow/blob/claude/project-thread-ct65o2/product/requirements/screen/cases/planng-night.21.19.png) (the picture animates between the two).

Choices I made that you might want different:
- **Late shows:** a show that runs past 01:00 still stretches the bottom to the hour it ends, so it's never cut off.
- **The evening before:** the 23:00 to midnight hour at the top of a day shows the hours only. It doesn't repeat the previous night's late shows.

Most calendar pictures changed with the new hours, and one test's drag gesture moved to keep clear of the day-start line. Its checks are the same. All 191 UI tests and `npm run verify` pass locally.

```
product/        new leaves 21.19 and 21.20; 21.6's note updated; the calendar pictures re-rendered
site/planNG/    the fixed axis, the night's + button and its remembered state
```

I added Ariel's fixed-hours change to PR #901 and replied in the thread. All 191 UI tests and `npm run verify` pass locally. CI hasn't reported on the new push yet.

- **Fixed hours:** every day now runs from 08:00 to 01:00 at one height. Moving the day's start or end only moves its line, so the calendar never resizes.
- **The night:** a big **+** in the corner above the hours opens the night from 23:00 the evening before, and **−** folds it back. It starts folded and the choice is remembered. While folded, the + shows a number when something falls in those hours, such as an early breakfast.
- **Two choices Ariel may want different:**
  - A show running past 01:00 still stretches the bottom of the calendar so it isn't cut off.
  - The 23:00–midnight hour at the top of a day shows only the hours. It doesn't repeat the previous night's late shows.
- **Pictures and tests:** 32 existing calendar pictures were re-rendered for the new hours. I spot-checked several.
- **Meal-drag test (28.7):** the test grabbed the meal where the day-start line's drag handle now sits on top of it. I moved its pointer lower on the block and left its checks unchanged.

The spec change went in as its own commit ahead of the code, and I rewrote the PR description to cover everything in it.

message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   - This is Ariel's (user_01KFq3mgDbJgesJHQomDhi72) "Calendar planning" thread for the PlanNG calendar planner (site/planNG/), worked as a sequence of PRs.
   - Merged PRs: #885, #891, #893, #894, #895, and #898 (airport-to-town, squash sha ad54cb2, merged after Ariel's "lgtm").
   - PR #901 (open, branch `claude/project-thread-ct65o2`) carries Ariel's planner feedback. It is done and pushed:
     - (a) Short shows are never drawn past the day end.
     - (b) Kept-day titles never overflow; adjacent same-type kept days merge under one title.
     - (c) Dragging a day edge holds every day's width.
     - (d) Shows animate in, out and across.
     - (e) "How full a day" takes 0 and up, with no cap.
     - (f) The festivals chip shows each festival's calendar stripe and distance, and lists out-of-reach festivals greyed out. The "km away" lines above the calendar are removed.
     - (g) Fixed hours from 08:00 to 01:00, with a "+" button in the gutter corner that opens the night from 23:00 the evening before. Folded by default, remembered, and it counts hidden items.
   - In progress (to add to #901): Ariel's hover card rework:
     - A 500ms delay before the card opens; hide it when the pointer leaves the card.
     - Remove all native HTML title tooltips.
     - A card for travel legs that says plainly, e.g., "walking 4 minutes from A to B". No map.
     - The four actions (lock, not this night, favourite, not this show) move to the top, emoji only, with better emojis. Hovering a button explains it.
     - A first-time tutorial hint telling the user to click these buttons; it is dropped for good once any button is pressed.
   - After that: go back to the list, starting with show pictures for the Haifa and Acco festivals (the scrapers). Restaurant suggestions are deferred.
   - Ariel's principle: top-level answers derive defaults, and a user's explicit choice always wins.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Executable spec in product/requirements.md, with cases in product/requirements/{screen,behavior,logic}/cases.
     - Screen goldens are pixel-exact (Playwright 1.56.1); animated goldens are APNG and compared by bytes.
     - Doc-first: commit the red spec before the code.
     - Refresh goldens with `node product/requirements/shared/refresh.js <filter>`.
     - Checks: `npm run test:ui`, `npm run verify`, and `node .claudinite/shared/engine/checks/check_the_work.mjs`.
     - Gallery markers: `![name](requirements/screen/cases/name.png) <!-- req-gallery:ID -->` for a picture, or `🚩 _Behavior leaf._ <!-- req-gallery:ID -->`.
     - Never reuse leaf numbers (21.8 is retired).
   - Harness:
     - `Element.prototype.animate` is stubbed: `finished` is `Promise.resolve()`, and `onfinish` fires via setTimeout, which a paused clock never runs. Ghost removal therefore uses `anim.finished.then`.
     - Desktop viewport is 1280×900.
     - Capture tools: `t.rectOf`, `t.union`, `t.pad`, `t.clip`, `t.unionClip`, `t.element`, `t.animate`.
   - i18n (site/planNG/i18n/translations.js):
     - Every entry needs `probe` + `maxWidthPx`, or `maxWidthPx: null` + `unrendered: "<reason>"`, in en/he/ru/ja.
     - Keys must be spelled out literally in source; the catalogue gate fails on template-built keys.
     - Regenerate localized pages with `node scripts/localize-pages.mjs`.
   - To look at the site locally: `python3 -m http.server 8000` from site/, with scratchpad Playwright scripts importing `/opt/node22/lib/node_modules/playwright/index.mjs`.
   - Git and GitHub:
     - Squash-only; no force-push (it was denied).
     - After a merge, reset with `git fetch origin main && git checkout -B claude/project-thread-ct65o2 origin/main`.
     - Commits end with `Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>` and `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_011xa2gBaZz9jyFL7YjmFqFs`.
     - PR bodies: Before/After/How, ending with the 🤖 Generated line and the session URL.
   - hearthbot conventions:
     - Only `mcp__hearthbot__*` calls reach the user.
     - Open the first reply after a session start with the "Loaded Claudinite…" line.
     - For an owner comment, open with a "Comment class:" line.
     - End replies with `> ✅ All done` or `> ⚠️ Still open: …`.
     - Include a folders-touched code box when handing over a PR.
     - "lgtm" means squash-merge with expectedHeadSha.
     - Don't poll PRs.
     - React 👀 on a user message, then unreact when the reply goes out.

3. Files and Code Sections (branch commits on top of origin/main):
   - Commits so far:
     - 565ac35 spec
     - 54f9101 fixes
     - cc5d484 spec 28.13/28.14
     - 54d70a6 kept runs
     - 113a289 spec 21.19/21.20
     - 28846aa fixed axis
   - **site/planNG/planNG.js**
     - Axis constants replace AXIS_PAD_MIN, ZONE_MAX_MIN and SCH_HOUR_MIN:
       ```js
       const AXIS_DAY_TOP_MIN = 8 * 60; const AXIS_NIGHT_TOP_MIN = -60; const AXIS_BOTTOM_MIN = 25 * 60;
       const SCH_AXIS_TARGET_PX = 780;
       const SCH_HOUR_PX = Math.round(SCH_AXIS_TARGET_PX / ((AXIS_BOTTOM_MIN - AXIS_DAY_TOP_MIN) / 60));
       ```
     - `calendarAxis(draft)`:
       - Uses the drag's held axis while a drag is in progress.
       - Otherwise the bottom is `max(25:00, latest slot/own end)` rounded up to the hour, and the top is `state.nightOpen ? -60 : 480`.
       - `axisOf` returns a fixed hourPx.
     - `nightToggle(draft)` builds a button `.sch-night[data-night]`:
       - Shows "+" or "−", with aria-label/title from `night.show` / `night.hide`.
       - `.sch-night-count` shows the number of slots and own blocks that start before 08:00 while folded.
       - It is appended to `.sch-gutter-head`.
       - A click handler in `wireDays` toggles `state.nightOpen`, then calls savePrefs and redraft, and refocuses the button.
     - `state.nightOpen` is saved in prefs and restored with `saved.nightOpen === true`.
     - Hour labels before 0 also get `sch-hour--late`.
     - Last-block ceiling:
       ```js
       const ceiling = Math.min(next ? y(next.startMinuteOfDay) - 2 : axisH, y(dayEndMin()));
       ```
     - Per-day count:
       - The input has `min="0"` and no max.
       - The handler: `const count = Math.round(Number(el.value)); state.maxPerDay = Number.isFinite(count) ? Math.max(0, count) : state.maxPerDay;`
       - Restore: `Number.isFinite(saved.maxPerDay) ? Math.max(0, saved.maxPerDay) : state.maxPerDay`.
     - Drag hold:
       - `holdLayout(ov)` returns `{topMin, botMin, slivers: Set of .sch-day--empty dates}`.
       - It is used by `startBlockerDrag` and the own-block drag.
       - The sliver class during a drag is `state.drag.slivers.has(iso)`.
     - Festivals chip (`festivalsHtml()`):
       - Rows are `label.pref-check.fest-row` containing a checkbox, `.fest-stripe[data-festival-colour]` and `.fest-words` (a `.pref-check-word` plus `.fest-km`).
       - The distance line uses `prefs.festivals.dayTrip` or `prefs.festivals.partly`.
       - Out-of-reach festivals are `div.pref-check.fest-row.fest-row--out`, with no input, showing `prefs.festivals.out`.
     - `renderPoolNote()` now shows only the `pool.noProgramme` line. The pool.also, pool.partly and pool.out keys were removed.
     - `keepBanner` and `keepBlock` wrap the name in `<span class="keep-name">`.
     - `titleKeptRuns(host)`:
       - Finds runs of adjacent columns with the same keep (same kind and festival).
       - Adds `sch-keep--run` plus `-first`, `-mid` or `-last` to each member's block.
       - Appends a `.sch-keep-title.sch-keep-title--<kind>` overlay (aria-hidden, pointer-events none) holding a clone of the first label, positioned over the run.
     - `renderCalendar`:
       - Calls `const before = snapshotCalendar(host)` before `innerHTML = ""`.
       - After `markColumnWidth()`, calls `titleKeptRuns(host); animateCalendar(host, before);`.
       - `buildTravelLeg` sets `leg.dataset.after = \`${a.slug}@${slotKey(a)}\``.
       - motion.js is imported after the arrival.js import.
     - Hover card code (read, not yet changed):
       - `openCardPop(block)` (~line 2281) builds the #calPreview innerHTML in this order: popArtHtml, title, where, about, link, rarity, the nights list, then `.pop-verdicts`.
       - The verdict helper renders `<button class="vb vb--kind" data-verdict aria-label title>` containing `.vb-mark` and `.vb-word`.
       - Current marks: lock "🔒", favourite "★", noTime "✕", noShow "⊘".
       - `wireCalendar()` (~line 2625): the click on `[data-verdict]` calls `applyVerdict(kind, pop.dataset.slug, pop.dataset.key)`.
       - `pointerover` on `.sch-show` opens the card immediately.
       - Close currently happens only on `wrap` pointerleave, or on popup pointerleave via `closeSoon` (220ms). This is the bug: the card stays open when you move off a block but stay inside the calendar.
       - Also wired: focusin, keydown (Enter/Space/ArrowDown), scroll → closePops, and Escape.
     - Native `title=` usages to remove:
       - line ~553 `seg.title` (perf.tip, a year strip/timeline segment; check whether it is in scope)
       - line 729 (pref pick tip)
       - line 768 (the suggested ✨ span)
       - line 1761 `btn.title` (my own night button)
       - line 2204 `leg.title = title` (the travel leg)
       - line 2314 (verdict buttons)
       - line 3522 (flight fare link)
   - **site/planNG/motion.js** (new):
     - `snapshotCalendar(host)` returns `{days: Map date→rect, blocks: Map key→{el,date,rect}}`.
     - Blocks are selected with `[".sch-slot",".sch-own",".sch-keep",".sch-leg"]` → `.sch-body > X:not(.sch-ghost)`.
     - `keyOf`:
       - `show:slug@key` for a slot
       - `own:` + own id or which (flights)
       - `keep:` + date
       - `leg:` + dataset.after
     - `animateCalendar(host, before)`:
       - Returns early if there is no before-state, if reduced motion is set, or if no dates overlap (another trip).
       - Measures everything first, then animates.
       - A day whose width changed animates its width (flex none).
       - A new block animates `{opacity:0, transform:"scale(0.85)"}` → none.
       - A moved block animates `translate(dx,dy)` → none, with dx relative to its day when the day is unchanged.
       - A block that left gets a ghost clone `.sch-ghost` in the same date's `.sch-body` at its old position, animating opacity 1 → 0, removed via `anim.finished.then(gone, gone)`.
       - MOVE_MS is 220, easing `cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)`.
   - **site/planNG/planNG.css**, additions:
     - `.sch-keep{overflow:hidden}`, `.keep-label{max-width:100%}`, `.keep-name` with ellipsis.
     - `.sch-keep--run` rules, and `.sch-keep-title` / `.sch-keep-title--festival`.
     - `.fest-stripe` (4px bar), `.fest-row`, `.fest-words`, `.fest-km`, `.fest-row--out` (opacity .6, padding-inline-start 21px).
     - `.sch-ghost{pointer-events:none;z-index:1}`.
     - `.sch-gutter-head` flex-centred, `.sch-night` (30px circle), `.sch-night-count` badge.
   - **site/planNG/i18n/translations.js**:
     - Added `prefs.festivals.dayTrip`, `.partly`, `.out`:
       - probe `.pref-check-word`, maxWidthPx 300.
       - en: "{km} km away · a day trip" / "· some nights" / "· too far", with he/ru/ja equivalents.
     - Added `night.show` / `night.hide` (unrendered).
     - Removed pool.also, pool.partly and pool.out.
   - **product/requirements.md**:
     - New leaves:
       - 21.15 (screen `planng-dayend-short`)
       - 21.16 (behavior `planng-drag-widths`)
       - 21.17 (behavior `planng-motion`)
       - 21.18 (behavior `planng-pace-any`)
       - 21.19 (screen `planng-night`, animated)
       - 21.20 (behavior `planng-night-kept`)
       - 28.13 "A kept day's title stays inside its own column, however narrow." (screen `planng-festival-banner`, desktop, `?from=2026-09-18&to=2026-10-08&festival=haifa-iff`)
       - 28.14 "Days in a row kept for the same thing join into one stretch under one title." (screen `planng-kept-run`, with localStorage `planNG.days` kept for Acco on 2026-09-29 and 2026-09-30)
     - Reworded 21.13, 23.5 ("named in the festivals chip, with how far it is"), and 21.6's notes.
   - **Cases changed**:
     - planng-out-of-reach.23.5: checks `#panel-festivals .fest-row--out` has text with "4,000 km", no input in the row, and no `#poolNote .pool-line`.
     - jerusalem-own-blocks.28.7: the drag now scrolls the meal to the start and then `scrollBy(0,-280)`, and grabs it at `from.y + from.height - 12`. Assertions are unchanged.
     - planng-drag-widths.21.16: uses the `.dl-grip` bounding box after `scrollIntoViewIfNeeded`, and asserts the flag text changed.
   - Goldens: 32 were re-rendered for the fixed axis, and others earlier. Latest local state: `npm run test:ui` 191/191 pass, verify is clean, and the work checks are clean.
   - /mnt/project-files/calendar-planning/design.md line 3 lists #898 as built, with "Next: show pictures for Haifa and Acco."

4. Errors and fixes:
   - Prefs were saved before `carChanged` in #898: reordered.
   - Budget failures on the new chip strings: shortened the strings and set the budget to 300.
   - Ghosts were counted as shows, and a lingering ghost key made a returning show animate as a move instead of growing in: ghosts are now excluded from snapshots and from the test selectors.
   - Ghosts persisted under the paused clock because `onfinish` never fired: removal now uses `anim.finished.then`.

1	/* The calendar is redrawn whole on every change, so without help a show that
2	 * leaves simply vanishes and one that arrives simply appears. This compares
3	 * what the calendar held before a redraw with what it holds after, and plays
4	 * the difference: a block still there slides from where it was, a new one
5	 * grows in, one that left is drawn once more where it stood and shrinks away,
6	 * and a day whose width changed eases to its new width.
7	 *
8	 * A block is known across redraws by what it is (a show's performance, a block
9	 * of the reader's own, a kept day's banner, the walk after a show), never by
10	 * its DOM node, which the redraw replaces.
11	 */
12	
13	const MOVE_MS = 220;
14	const EASE = "cubic-bezier(0.2, 0, 0, 1)";
15	
16	function keyOf(el) {
17	  if (el.classList.contains("sch-slot")) {
18	    const show = el.querySelector(".sch-show");
19	    return show ? `show:${show.dataset.slug}@${show.dataset.key}` : null;
20	  }
21	  if (el.classList.contains("sch-own")) return `own:${el.dataset.own || el.dataset.which}`;
22	  if (el.classList.contains("sch-keep")) return `keep:${el.dataset.keep}`;
23	  if (el.classList.contains("sch-leg")) return el.dataset.after ? `leg:${el.dataset.after}` : null;
24	  return null;
25	}
26	
27	const BLOCKS = [".sch-slot", ".sch-own", ".sch-keep", ".sch-leg"].map((c) => `.sch-body > ${c}:not(.sch-ghost)`).join(", ");
28	
29	/** Where everything on the calendar is now, to be played from after a redraw. */
30	export function snapshotCalendar(host) {
31	  const days = new Map();
32	  for (const col of host.querySelectorAll(".sch-day")) days.set(col.dataset.date, col.getBoundingClientRect());
33	  const blocks = new Map();
34	  for (const el of host.querySelectorAll(BLOCKS)) {
35	    const key = keyOf(el);
36	    if (!key) continue;
37	    const date = el.closest(".sch-day").dataset.date;
38	    blocks.set(key, { el, date, rect: el.getBoundingClientRect() });
39	  }
40	  return { days, blocks };
41	}
42	
43	/** Play the calendar from `before` to what it holds now. */
44	export function animateCalendar(host, before) {
45	  if (!before || !before.blocks.size) return;
46	  if (matchMedia("(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)").matches) return;
47	  const timing = { duration: MOVE_MS, easing: EASE };
48	
49	  // Everything is measured before anything is animated: a day easing to a new
50	  // width moves the layout, and a measure after it would force another.
51	  const dayNow = new Map();
52	  for (const col of host.querySelectorAll(".sch-day")) dayNow.set(col.dataset.date, { col, rect: col.getBoundingClientRect() });
53	  // A calendar of other days entirely (another trip) is a new calendar, not
54	  // this one changing: it is drawn, not played.
55	  if (![...dayNow.keys()].some((date) => before.days.has(date))) return;
56	  const now = [];
57	  for (const el of host.querySelectorAll(BLOCKS)) {
58	    const key = keyOf(el);
59	    if (key) now.push({ el, key, date: el.closest(".sch-day").dataset.date, rect: el.getBoundingClientRect() });
60	  }
61	  const bodies = new Map();
62	  for (const [date, { col }] of dayNow) {
63	    const body = col.querySelector(".sch-body");
64	    if (body) bodies.set(date, { body, rect: body.getBoundingClientRect() });
65	  }
66	
67	  // A day whose width changed eases to it; a block's slide is measured
68	  // against its own day, so the day carries its blocks with it.
69	  for (const [date, { col, rect }] of dayNow) {
70	    const was = before.days.get(date);
71	    if (!was || Math.abs(was.width - rect.width) <= 0.5) continue;
72	    col.animate(
73	      [
74	        { flex: "0 0 auto", width: `${was.width}px`, minWidth: "0px", maxWidth: "none" },
75	        { flex: "0 0 auto", width: `${rect.width}px`, minWidth: "0px", maxWidth: "none" },
76	      ],
77	      timing
78	    );
79	  }
80	
81	  const seen = new Set();
82	  for (const { el, key, date, rect } of now) {
83	    seen.add(key);
84	    const was = before.blocks.get(key);
85	    if (!was) {
86	      el.animate([{ opacity: 0, transform: "scale(0.85)" }, { opacity: 1, transform: "none" }], timing);
87	      continue;
88	    }
89	    // Within one day, against the day's own edge; across days, on the page.
90	    const sameDay = was.date === date && before.days.has(date);
91	    const dx = sameDay
92	      ? was.rect.left - before.days.get(date).left - (rect.left - dayNow.get(date).rect.left)
93	      : was.rect.left - rect.left;
94	    const dy = was.rect.top - rect.top;
95	    if (Math.abs(dx) < 0.5 && Math.abs(dy) < 0.5) continue;
96	    el.animate([{ transform: `translate(${dx}px, ${dy}px)` }, { transform: "none" }], timing);
97	  }
98	
99	  // What left is drawn once more, in the day it left, and shrinks away there.
100	  for (const [key, was] of before.blocks) {
101	    if (seen.has(key)) continue;
102	    const at = bodies.get(was.date);
103	    if (!at) continue;
104	    const ghost = was.el.cloneNode(true);
105	    ghost.classList.add("sch-ghost");
106	    ghost.setAttribute("aria-hidden", "true");
107	    ghost.removeAttribute("tabindex");
108	    for (const focusable of ghost.querySelectorAll("[tabindex], a, button")) focusable.setAttribute("tabindex", "-1");
109	    ghost.style.inset = "auto";
110	    Object.assign(ghost.style, {
111	      top: `${was.rect.top - at.rect.top}px`,
112	      left: `${was.rect.left - at.rect.left}px`,
113	      width: `${was.rect.width}px`,
114	      height: `${was.rect.height}px`,
115	    });
116	    at.body.appendChild(ghost);
117	    const anim = ghost.animate([{ opacity: 1, transform: "none" }, { opacity: 0, transform: "scale(0.85)" }], timing);
118	    const gone = () => ghost.remove();
119	    anim.finished.then(gone, gone);
120	  }
121	}

Base directory for this skill: /home/claude/EdFringeNow/.claude/skills/requirements-harness

# The requirements harness

The framework conventions are the `executable-requirements` pack and the judgment layer is
`spec-driven-product` plus the `writing-tests` skill; layout, lanes and commands are
`product/requirements/README.md`. This carries what those don't: a Playwright golden harness,
and the local approval and fixture policy.

## Writing the spec

- **Laying out `product/requirements.md`** — under each visual leaf its golden is visible and
  uncollapsed; every textual expansion (acceptance notes, proof pointers) is collapsed in a
  `<details>` block. The document is read by sight.

- **Writing a visual leaf's statement** — one line saying what is asserted; the golden carries
  the copy, counts, colours and placement. Anything not visible (a threshold, the rule behind
  the state) goes in a collapsed **Notes** block. (visual-leafs-statement)

- **Choosing a golden's capture** — the smallest surface that proves the leaf: an element crop,
  a clipped region, or a stitched composite, never the whole page or control. The recipe lives on
  the case (`capture: "<selector>"` or `capture(page, tools)`, see `shared/capture-tools.js`);
  whole-page capture is a deliberate exception. (golden-smallest-surface)

- **Proving what an action changes** — capture the same region before and after (and after a
  reload where persistence is the point) and play them as one animated golden (`tools.animate`);
  keep `stitchV`/`stitchH` for things genuinely side by side. (change-time-animation)

- **Encoding an animated golden** — APNG, never GIF (`shared/png.js`'s `encodeAnimated`); the
  comparator compares an animated golden's bytes only. (animated-golden-apng)

- **Placing a leaf both pages follow** — the spec is organised by what the product does, never by
  code layout: a cross-page rule is one feature whose picture shows both the Now page and the
  planner, in the cross-page part after the two page-by-page segments. A case may navigate
  between pages, or open a second page when something fixed at context creation must differ.

- **About to route a leaf to `behavior` or `logic`** — first ask whether it decomposes into
  observable states; a statement joined by "and" usually does, and each part becomes its own
  numbered sub-leaf with its own picture, the parent a heading. When a leaf lands in a coded kind
  because the product makes it invisible, say so in its Notes and name the product change that
  would make it visual.

- **Using `behavior`** — for a gesture's outgoing consequence (a URL built, bytes downloaded,
  storage written) or what the OS paints rather than the page (a native `title` tooltip, a
  cursor). (behavior-rule)

- **Using `logic`** — for a pure rule with no rendered surface; when it is about how values are
  written, declare `table: { columns, rows }` so the gallery renders the table and `verify()`
  proves every row. (logic-rule)

## The browser is part of the expected

- **Bumping the pinned Playwright** — it re-renders every golden, so it is a re-baselining,
  approved like one: the harness refuses any other version (`shared/harness/browser.js`).

- **A comparison that flaps** — add determinism, never a tolerance; the comparator stays at zero
  diff, and the levers (fixed clock, geolocation, seeded `Math.random`, route-fulfilled network,
  frozen animations, render flags) all live in the harness.

## Traps the harness already paid for

- **Serving the fake origin** — keep it `https://`: geolocation exists only on secure origins,
  and on plain http the app keeps its simulated clock and renders the wrong day.
  (geolocation-exists-only)

- **Moving or denying the fixed geolocation** — the app adopts the device clock only on an
  in-UK fix, so anywhere else renders its pre-set simulated moment, a different day file.
  (app-adopts-device)

- **Captures racing the planner's board animation** — a CSS freeze doesn't stop
  `element.animate`; the harness stubs it to land on end states. (css-freeze-does)

- **Text shifting by a pixel everywhere** — the vendored `fonts.css` resolves against
  `fonts.googleapis.com`, so the vendor route matches on path, host-agnostic. (fonts-arrive-google)

- **Adding an emoji, symbol or script to the product or fixtures** — rebuild the
  `harness/vendor/systemfonts/` subset (its README): Chromium runs under a `FONTCONFIG_FILE`
  that sees only that directory, and a missing glyph renders as tofu. (vendoring-web-fonts)

- **Reproducing a golden flake locally** — compare with the harness's `compare.js`, never a byte
  hash: PNG bytes differ across identical renders, and CI enforces pixels.
  (reproducing-golden-flake)

- **A red `ui-requirements` lane** — its artifact downloads from a host the proxy denies, so read
  which case failed from `get_job_logs` (large `tail_lines`) and re-run it locally;
  `npm run test:ui` writes `.actual.png` / `.diff.png` into `shared/.artifacts/`. (red-ci-lanes)

- **Capturing a floating popup** — set `viewportOnly: true`: a full-page capture scrolls, and
  scrolling dismisses tips, legends and pops. (floating-popup-dies)

- **Waiting for a page to be ready** — wait on the observable state the pages settle into (the
  footer version popup's text, the search placeholder's show count; `case-helpers.js`) plus
  `document.fonts.ready`, never `networkidle`. (ready-networkidle)

- **Capturing hover-driven UI** — open it inside `capture()`, not `drive()`: the runner settles
  the scroll between them, and the scroll fires `mouseleave`. (hover-driven-ui)

## The fixture freeze

- **Needing data for a case** — use `shared/fixtures/data/`, a frozen snapshot of the real
  committed data cast by the committed builder for state variety; never reach for `site/data/`.
  Every deviation from the source bytes is an `ADJUST` in the builder.

- **Re-running the builder** — it re-casts every golden, so run it only with the owner's
  approval and land builder, fixtures, goldens and gallery in one reviewed change.

- **Having invoked `build-fixtures.js` at all**, even against a scratch edit — it writes into
  `fixtures/data/` as it goes, so `git diff --stat` the whole fixtures dir before deciding there
  is nothing to revert. (build-fixtures-partial-drift)

## Golden approval

- **A golden that no longer matches** — show the owner the committed golden beside
  `shared/.artifacts/<case>.actual.png` and `.diff.png` through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, one
  per item, and say so in the PR body.

- **Landing an intended UI change** — spec edit (doc-first, red), then the implementation, then
  `npm run refresh:ui`, with the refreshed PNGs in the same diff.

  code layout: a cross-page rule is one feature whose picture shows both the Now page and the
  planner, in the cross-page part after the two page-by-page segments. A case may navigate
  between pages, or open a second page when something fixed at context creation must differ.

- **About to route a leaf to `behavior` or `logic`** — first ask whether it decomposes into
  observable states; a statement joined by "and" usually does, and each part becomes its own
  numbered sub-leaf with its own picture, the parent a heading. When a leaf lands in a coded kind
  because the product makes it invisible, say so in its Notes and name the product change that
  would make it visual.

- **Using `behavior`** — for a gesture's outgoing consequence (a URL built, bytes downloaded,
  storage written) or what the OS paints rather than the page (a native `title` tooltip, a
  cursor). (behavior-rule)

- **Using `logic`** — for a pure rule with no rendered surface; when it is about how values are
  written, declare `table: { columns, rows }` so the gallery renders the table and `verify()`
  proves every row. (logic-rule)

## The browser is part of the expected

- **Bumping the pinned Playwright** — it re-renders every golden, so it is a re-baselining,
  approved like one: the harness refuses any other version (`shared/harness/browser.js`).

- **A comparison that flaps** — add determinism, never a tolerance; the comparator stays at zero
  diff, and the levers (fixed clock, geolocation, seeded `Math.random`, route-fulfilled network,
  frozen animations, render flags) all live in the harness.

## Traps the harness already paid for

- **Serving the fake origin** — keep it `https://`: geolocation exists only on secure origins,
  and on plain http the app keeps its simulated clock and renders the wrong day.
  (geolocation-exists-only)

- **Moving or denying the fixed geolocation** — the app adopts the device clock only on an
  in-UK fix, so anywhere else renders its pre-set simulated moment, a different day file.
  (app-adopts-device)

- **Captures racing the planner's board animation** — a CSS freeze doesn't stop
  `element.animate`; the harness stubs it to land on end states. (css-freeze-does)

- **Text shifting by a pixel everywhere** — the vendored `fonts.css` resolves against
  `fonts.googleapis.com`, so the vendor route matches on path, host-agnostic. (fonts-arrive-google)

- **Adding an emoji, symbol or script to the product or fixtures** — rebuild the
  `harness/vendor/systemfonts/` subset (its README): Chromium runs under a `FONTCONFIG_FILE`
  that sees only that directory, and a missing glyph renders as tofu. (vendoring-web-fonts)

- **Reproducing a golden flake locally** — compare with the harness's `compare.js`, never a byte
  hash: PNG bytes differ across identical renders, and CI enforces pixels.
  (reproducing-golden-flake)

- **A red `ui-requirements` lane** — its artifact downloads from a host the proxy denies, so read
  which case failed from `get_job_logs` (large `tail_lines`) and re-run it locally;
  `npm run test:ui` writes `.actual.png` / `.diff.png` into `shared/.artifacts/`. (red-ci-lanes)

- **Capturing a floating popup** — set `viewportOnly: true`: a full-page capture scrolls, and
  scrolling dismisses tips, legends and pops. (floating-popup-dies)

- **Waiting for a page to be ready** — wait on the observable state the pages settle into (the
  footer version popup's text, the search placeholder's show count; `case-helpers.js`) plus
  `document.fonts.ready`, never `networkidle`. (ready-networkidle)

- **Capturing hover-driven UI** — open it inside `capture()`, not `drive()`: the runner settles
  the scroll between them, and the scroll fires `mouseleave`. (hover-driven-ui)

## The fixture freeze

- **Needing data for a case** — use `shared/fixtures/data/`, a frozen snapshot of the real
  committed data cast by the committed builder for state variety; never reach for `site/data/`.
  Every deviation from the source bytes is an `ADJUST` in the builder.

- **Re-running the builder** — it re-casts every golden, so run it only with the owner's
  approval and land builder, fixtures, goldens and gallery in one reviewed change.

- **Having invoked `build-fixtures.js` at all**, even against a scratch edit — it writes into
  `fixtures/data/` as it goes, so `git diff --stat` the whole fixtures dir before deciding there
  is nothing to revert. (build-fixtures-partial-drift)

## Golden approval

- **A golden that no longer matches** — show the owner the committed golden beside
  `shared/.artifacts/<case>.actual.png` and `.diff.png` through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, one
  per item, and say so in the PR body.

- **Landing an intended UI change** — spec edit (doc-first, red), then the implementation, then
  `npm run refresh:ui`, with the refreshed PNGs in the same diff.

</system-reminder>

## Claude_Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>

<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>

<?claude block s1?>

<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.
